  "extract_plan": {
    "chunk_summary": "Table ES 1 defines twelve dimensions of data quality under three domains (Utility, Objectivity, Integrity); the following text asserts how threats to data quality differ for single-source versus integrated data products and gives best practices for identifying and reporting them."
  },
  "concepts": [
    {"id": "c_relevance", "name": "Relevance", "aliases": [], "description": "Data quality dimension in the Utility domain concerning whether a data product meets current and prospective user needs.", "anchor": "Relevance refers to whether", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_accessibility", "name": "Accessibility", "aliases": [], "description": "Data quality dimension concerning the ease with which users can obtain products and documentation.", "anchor": "Accessibility relates to the ease", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_timeliness", "name": "Timeliness", "aliases": [], "description": "Data quality dimension concerning the lag between the phenomenon described and data availability.", "anchor": "Timeliness is the length of time", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_punctuality", "name": "Punctuality", "aliases": [], "description": "Data quality dimension concerning the lag between actual release and the planned target release date.", "anchor": "Punctuality is measured as the time lag", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_granularity", "name": "Granularity", "aliases": [], "description": "Data quality dimension concerning the amount of disaggregation available for key data elements.", "anchor": "Granularity refers to the amount of disaggregation", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_accuracy", "name": "Accuracy", "aliases": [], "description": "Data quality dimension in the Objectivity domain measuring closeness of an estimate to its true value.", "anchor": "Accuracy measures the closeness", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_reliability", "name": "Reliability", "aliases": [], "description": "Concept related to accuracy, characterizing consistency of results under repeated measurement.", "anchor": "Reliability, a related concept", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_coherence", "name": "Coherence", "aliases": [], "description": "Data quality dimension concerning common definitions, classification, alignment with external statistical standards, and comparability.", "anchor": "Coherence is defned as the ability", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_scientific_integrity", "name": "Scientifc integrity", "aliases": ["Scientific integrity"], "description": "Data quality dimension in the Integrity domain concerning adherence to scientific standards and insulation from inappropriate political influence.", "anchor": "Scientifc integrity refers to an environment", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_credibility", "name": "Credibility", "aliases": [], "description": "Data quality dimension concerning user confidence based on the producer's qualifications and past performance.", "anchor": "Credibility characterizes the confdence", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_computer_physical_security", "name": "Computer and physical security", "aliases": [], "description": "Data quality dimension concerning protection of information from unauthorized access or revision throughout the production process.", "anchor": "physical security of data refers", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_confidentiality", "name": "Confdentiality", "aliases": ["Confidentiality"], "description": "Data quality dimension concerning the obligation not to disclose information to an unauthorized party.", "anchor": "Confdentiality refers to a quality or condition", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_utility", "name": "Utility", "aliases": [], "description": "Domain of data quality covering relevance, accessibility, timeliness, punctuality, and granularity.", "anchor": "Utility", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_objectivity", "name": "Objectivity", "aliases": [], "description": "Domain of data quality covering accuracy and reliability, and coherence.", "anchor": "Objectivity", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_integrity", "name": "Integrity", "aliases": [], "description": "Domain of data quality covering scientific integrity, credibility, computer and physical security, and confidentiality.", "anchor": "Integrity", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_threats", "name": "threats to data quality", "aliases": ["quality threats"], "description": "Conditions that degrade the quality of a data collection, data product, or output, to be identified and minimized.", "anchor": "Best practices to identify threats to data quality", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_integrated", "name": "integrated data products", "aliases": ["integrated data"], "description": "Data products built from multiple input sources, inheriting each source's quality threats plus threats from integration.", "anchor": "quality threats for integrated data products include", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_integration_method", "name": "integration method", "aliases": [], "description": "The method by which sources are combined into an integrated data product, including record linkage, modeling, and harmonization.", "anchor": "the integration method, including record linkage", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "c_quality_reporting", "name": "Quality reporting", "aliases": ["reporting data quality"], "description": "Documentation of data quality, ranging from detailed technical documentation to footnotes on a published statistic.", "anchor": "Quality reporting can take many forms", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"}

  "definitions": [
    {"id": "d_relevance", "term": "Relevance", "verbatim_text": "Relevance refers to whether the data product is targeted to meet current and prospective user needs.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Relevance refers to whether", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_accessibility", "term": "Accessibility", "verbatim_text": "Accessibility relates to the ease with which data users can obtain an agency’s products and documentation in forms and formats that are understandable to data users.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Accessibility relates to the ease", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_timeliness", "term": "Timeliness", "verbatim_text": "Timeliness is the length of time between the event or phenomenon the data describe and their availability.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Timeliness is the length of time", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_punctuality", "term": "Punctuality", "verbatim_text": "Punctuality is measured as the time lag between the actual release of the data and the planned target date for data release.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Punctuality is measured as the time lag", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_granularity", "term": "Granularity", "verbatim_text": "Granularity refers to the amount of disaggregation available for key data elements.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Granularity refers to the amount of disaggregation", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_accuracy", "term": "Accuracy", "verbatim_text": "Accuracy measures the closeness of an estimate from a data product to its true value.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Accuracy measures the closeness", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_reliability", "term": "Reliability", "verbatim_text": "Reliability, a related concept, characterizes the consistency of results when the same phenomenon is measured or estimated more than once under similar conditions.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Reliability, a related concept", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_coherence", "term": "Coherence", "verbatim_text": "Coherence is defned as the ability of the data product to maintain common defnitions, classifcation, and methodological processes, to align with external statistical standards, and to maintain consistency and comparability with other relevant data.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Coherence is defned as the ability", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_scientific_integrity", "term": "Scientifc integrity", "verbatim_text": "Scientifc integrity refers to an environment that ensures adherence to scientifc standards and use of established scientifc methods to produce and disseminate objective data products and one that shields these products from inappropriate political infuence.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Scientifc integrity refers to an environment", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_credibility", "term": "Credibility", "verbatim_text": "Credibility characterizes the confdence that users place in data products based simply on the qualifcations and past performance of the data producer.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Credibility characterizes the confdence", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_computer_physical_security", "term": "Computer and physical security", "verbatim_text": "Computer and physical security of data refers to the protection of information throughout the collection, production, analysis, and development process from unauthorized access or revision to ensure that the information is not compromised through corruption or falsifcation.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "physical security of data refers", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"},
    {"id": "d_confidentiality", "term": "Confdentiality", "verbatim_text": "Confdentiality refers to a quality or condition of information as an obligation not to disclose that information to an unauthorized party.", "normative_status": "policy", "as_of_date": null, "anchor": "Confdentiality refers to a quality or condition", "location": "fcsm-20-04-a-framework-for-data-quality#c0005"}
